findings: Payment-membership transaction gap — if POST /api/Membership fails after POST /api/Payment succeeds, the payment record orphans and the user loses money. Wrap both calls in a backend transaction or implement compensating deletion of the payment record on membership creation failure.

QR payment is cosmetic — the QR modal shows a placeholder emoji and a 'confirm' button that bypasses payment verification entirely. The feature will mislead users into thinking payment was processed. Either integrate a real QR payment provider or add prominent UI text clarifying this is a simulation.

localStorage schedule persistence won't sync — registrations saved in localStorage will disappear on cache clear, device switch, or browser change. Replace with backend persistence (e.g., POST /api/ScheduleRegistration endpoint) or document this as a known limitation.

No capacity enforcement on registration — the UI shows max capacity but never checks current enrollment before allowing registration. A popular class could exceed capacity with no warning. Add a backend capacity check or at least a frontend warning based on enrollment count.

Check-in QR code is never validated — any string passed to /api/Checkin/qr will be accepted by the frontend logic. If the backend doesn't validate format or freshness, users could fabricate check-ins. Confirm backend validation exists or add frontend format checking.
